Unit 1 of 10: History of Trade and Commerce in India

Key ideas

  • Ancient India had flourishing trade by land (Silk Route, Uttarapatha) and sea (ports such as Muziris, Tamralipti, Bharuch).
  • Indigenous banking: hundis (bills of exchange) and chitthis; moneylenders and seths provided credit and remittance. Types of hundi included dhani-jog, sah-jog, firman-jog, jokhmi.
  • Intermediaries (commission agents, brokers, distributors) and merchant communities (e.g. guilds — shreni) supported trade; trade centres included Pataliputra, Taxila, Ujjain, Surat, Kanchi, Madurai.
  • India was a major exporter of spices, textiles (muslin, silk), indigo and precious stones; the term "golden bird" reflects its prosperity. Colonial rule turned India into a supplier of raw materials and a market for British goods.

Worked examples

Example 1: What was a hundi? Answer: an indigenous bill of exchange/credit instrument used for remittance and credit in trade.

10-mark practice set

  1. (1 mark, MCQ) A hundi was a: (a) coin (b) bill of exchange (c) temple (d) port. Answer: (b).
  2. (1 mark) Name one ancient Indian port. Answer: Muziris (or Tamralipti, Bharuch).
  3. (2 marks) State two features of indigenous banking in ancient India. Answer: use of hundis/chitthis for credit and remittance (1); moneylenders and seths financing trade (1).
  4. (3 marks) Explain the role of intermediaries in ancient trade. Answer: commission agents and brokers linked buyers and sellers (1); distributors helped goods reach distant markets (1); they bore risks and extended credit (1).
  5. (3 marks) How did colonial rule change India's position in world trade? Answer: from exporter of finished goods (textiles) (1); to supplier of raw materials (1); and a market for British manufactured goods (1).

Common mistakes

  1. Hundi as currency. 2. Mixing ports and inland centres. 3. Ignoring guilds. 4. No colonial impact. 5. Vague examples.

Quick recall

  1. Hundi? 2. Guild? 3. Major export? 4. Southern port? 5. "Golden bird" means?

Answers: 1) Bill of exchange. 2) Shreni. 3) Textiles/spices. 4) Muziris. 5) Prosperous India.
